newsitem.title: INDIA: Institutional buying lifts Delhi shares near close.
newsitem.headline: Institutional buying lifts Delhi shares near close.

text.p: Selective buying by foreign and domestic financial institutions pushed up share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange on Tuesday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 6.25 points higher at 882.45.

Traders said the rise in share prices was temporary as they were awaiting the verdict of the Supreme Court, India's highest court of law, on former Bihar chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav's bail petition, before making long term commitments.

"Though stocks staged a partial recovery, it is very difficult to predict any definite trends of the market amid prevailing political uncertainty," said Rakesh Bhutani of stock brokers Vaishisht Securities.
The Supreme Court dismissed Yadav's plea against a state court's order not granting him "anticipatory bail" in a corruption case. The decision came after the close of trade on Tuesday,
Yadav has been indicted by federal police in a $280 million dollar scandal over embezzlement of state agricultural funds. He says he is innocent.
Traders added share prices were drifting lower in kerb dealings.
ITC closed 8.50 rupees higher at 484.50 on strong buying by foreign institutional investors, brokers said.
Bajaj Auto ended 28.00 rupees higher at 905.00.
Reliance Industries ended 1.65 rupees higher at 354.25.
Hindustan Lever closed 14.00 rupees higher at 1,380.00.
State Bank of India bucked the trend to close 0.40 rupee lower at 317.35.
